title: FLAG: Flow Policy MaxEnt-RL by Latent Augmented Guidance
claim: Baseline samplers collapse into noise as the sample budget shrinks, while ours still recovers the optimal multi-modal policy.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, method-by-sample-budget grids beside value-function insets
description: The figure is a wide strip of heatmaps in a green-yellow-blue colormap. On the far left is the optimal value function V* for a multi-goal point-mass task. It shows four target icons arranged in a diamond, with a red star and a purple star marking two states. Next to it, a small Q* heatmap sits in a purple frame. A larger purple-framed grid follows, with columns for SDAC, DPMD, QVPO, MaxEnt DP and FLAG (ours), and rows for N=32, 8 and 2. These cells show the policy at the purple-star state. A second Q* inset and policy grid, in red, show the policy at the red-star state. At N=32 most methods show the modes. At N=8 and N=2 the baselines become blobby and noisy, while the FLAG column keeps sharp multi-modal structure. The coloured frames link each state to its policy grid.
caption: Comparisons with global policy sampling methods in multi-goal environment. The multi-goal environment [ref] tasks a point mass with navigating to one of four symmetrically placed targets \raisebox{-0.2em}{\includegraphics[height=1.0em]{figures/multigoal/goal.png}}. We plot the optimal value function $V^*$ and Q-functions $Q^*$ at two different states (\raisebox{-0.2em}{\includegraphics[height=1.0em]{figures/multigoal/marker_3_3.png}} & \raisebox{-0.2em}{\includegraphics[height=1.0em]{figures/multigoal/marker_0_0.png}}), along with policies at each state. While other methods fail to learn with fewer samples $(N \le 8)$, FLAG captures optimal and multi-modal behaviors leveraging latent-augmented guidance, even in limited importance sample budget commonly arising in high-dimensional action spaces. Additional details on the environment and setup, along with statistics that quantify the local-IS mechanism, are presented in Appendix [ref].
abstract: Maximum entropy reinforcement learning (MaxEnt-RL) enables robust exploration, yet practical implementations often restrict policies to simple Gaussians. While recent approaches incorporate expressive generative policies via importance-weighted supervised learning, they are prone to importance weight collapse, which limits their scalability in high-dimensional action spaces. Our key insight is to mitigate this limitation by localizing the sampling region, avoiding the weight degeneracy induced by importance sampling over the entire action space. To instantiate this insight, we introduce \textbf{FLAG} (\textbf{F}low policy with \textbf{L}atent-\textbf{A}ugmented \textbf{G}uidance). FLAG augments the state space with a flow latent variable and optimizes a provably consistent proxy MaxEnt-RL objective. We empirically demonstrate that FLAG enables expressive policy optimization with limited importance samples and scales to state-based high-dimensional control tasks. Furthermore, FLAG achieves state-of-the-art performance among expressive-policy MaxEnt online RL methods on state-based high-dimensional control benchmarks.
